cells.tense: You're here, right now, and this one is yours to steer.
cells.verb: feeling the whole of what's connected arrive at once
cells.place: in the middle of a half-lit situation where the outcome isn't written
cells.ask: offer to keep knowing it rather than to finish knowing it — when you stop needing the answer to settle, the depth is what comes back.
cells.core: There's a moment you suddenly feel the whole thing at once — the room, the people, the current running between all of it — and instead of it wrecking you, it holds. Not a peak you're chasing, an arrival already here. You didn't force the clarity; you just stayed long enough to receive it.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel the whole thing without needing it decided.

cells.tense: You're already living at the end of a story that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: reaching for the whole feeling before it's assembled
cells.place: at the far edge of a situation you're trying to close early
cells.ask: hand the excess to a clear choice made from where you actually stand — when you choose from the present instead of the imagined end, the whole you were chasing comes back in pieces you can hold.
cells.core: You keep trying to bring the ending forward — deciding what it all means, what everyone feels, where it lands — before any of it has actually happened. The wholeness you're after can't be assembled in advance. The more you reach for it, the more you're standing in a future nobody's living yet, and the present goes unfelt behind you.
cells.sheetLine: You're finishing the story before it's been lived.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's behind you, and you know it.
cells.verb: feeling the whole of what's connected arrive at once
cells.place: in a situation you've stopped letting yourself step into
cells.ask: ask for the smallest fresh spark — one unplanned openness, before any of it means anything — and the connection you've been withholding comes back as it arrives.
cells.core: You've been holding yourself back from letting it land — the moment comes and you don't quite step in, so it passes you. It isn't that you can't feel the whole connection; it's that you've stayed on the far side of the room while everyone else is in it, waiting for a version of this that's already gone. The door isn't ahead of you.
cells.sheetLine: You know what it is. You're just not walking in.

cells.tense: You're already doing it — you just haven't signed for it.
cells.verb: feeling the whole of what's connected arrive at once
cells.place: in a situation you keep calling unclear
cells.ask: see that you already know it, in the simplest unspoken way — and when you stop calling it undecided, the knowledge you're already carrying comes back as something you can stand on.
cells.core: You keep saying this is still open, still unclear, still forming — but you already know how it feels, and you know it in your gut before your words catch up. You've been holding the truth quietly and handing the authority to the situation itself, as if the knowing were happening to you rather than by you.
cells.sheetLine: You already know how this feels. You keep calling it undecided.
